note: July 2026 intake (BI #350019 + Mary's Heirloom) in loader packet shape for 0b-load-seeds.mjs.

packets.name: Purple Plum Radish Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 4-6 wks before last frost through spring, then again late summer; succession every 1-2 wks
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow from early-mid April in the South Deerfield valley (a few weeks later in the Conway hilltown) as soon as soil is workable; light frost tolerant. Fast enough for repeated spring sowings and an excellent fall crop sown late August-September.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Round purple-skinned root with crisp mild-sweet white flesh; direct-sow only (dislikes transplant); bolt-prone and pithy in summer heat, so grow in cool spring/fall; edible root.

packets.name: Atomic Red Carrot Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 2-4 wks before last frost through early summer; succession every 2-3 wks
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow late April onward (dislikes transplant); keep the seedbed evenly moist through the slow germination. Color deepens with cooking and roots sweeten after fall frost, so a late-summer sowing for autumn harvest works well here.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Imperator-type 8-10 in. red root rich in lycopene, color intensifies when cooked; direct-sow only (taproot dislikes transplant); needs loose deep soil and steady moisture to germinate; edible root.

packets.name: Clancy Potato Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors ~6 wks before May 20 (early April). Transplant after last frost; potatoes need ~4 months to mature, targeting Sept–Oct harvest before first fall frost (Oct 1). True seed potatoes are disease-free compared to seed tubers.
sow_profile.packet_notes: True botanical potato seed (not tuber) — AAS winner, bred by Peter van Hest. Creamer-style potato with fine, versatile texture. Start in trays; transplant like tomatoes. Sterile seeds prevent disease transmission. Harvest as 'creamers' or let mature for full-size storage.

packets.name: Touchstone Gold Beet Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 3-4 wks before last frost when soil ≥50°F; succession every 3 wks through early summer
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow late April (valley) or early May (Conway) for June–July harvest. Can succession sow into July for fall roots. Tolerates light frost; golden flesh doesn't bleed like red beets.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Dislikes transplanting — direct sow only. Each seed is a multi-germ cluster; thin to 3"–4". Golden flesh holds color when cooked. Improved germination over older golden types.

packets.name: Gourmet Blend Beet Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 2-4 wks before last frost through midsummer; succession every 2-3 wks
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow from late April; beets tolerate light frost and transplant better than most roots, so an indoor start 4-6 wks ahead is optional for an early crop. Sow again in July-early August for fall harvest; thinnings are edible greens.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Heirloom blend of three types (deep red, pink-and-white striped Chioggia-style, and golden-orange roots); each 'seed' is a cluster so thin seedlings; edible root and greens; soaking seed overnight speeds germination.

packets.name: French Breakfast Radish Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 4-6 wks before last frost through spring, then again late summer; succession every 1-2 wks
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow from early-mid April in the valley (later up in Conway) once soil is workable; tolerates light frost and some summer heat but grows best cool. Ideal for spring and fall succession sowings.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Heirloom oblong scarlet root with white tip, delicate mild flavor; direct-sow only (dislikes transplant); bolt-prone in heat; pull promptly at size to avoid pithiness; edible root.

packets.name: Danvers 126 Carrot Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 2-4 wks before last frost through midsummer; succession every 2-3 wks
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow late April onward; its tolerance of heavy soils makes it forgiving in our valley clay loams. Sow again in July for a fall harvest that sweetens after frost; keep seedbed moist during slow germination.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Organic heirloom Massachusetts-bred 6-7 in. tapered root, high-fiber, heat-tolerant and resists cracking/splitting; performs in heavy soils; direct-sow only (dislikes transplant); edible root.

packets.name: Little Finger Carrot Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 2-4 wks before last frost through midsummer; succession every 2-3 wks
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow late April onward; the short 3 in. root suits our shallower or rockier hilltown beds and containers. Quick maturity allows several spring-through-fall sowings; harvest young and tender for pickling.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Baby Nantes-type 3 in. blunt cylindrical root bred in France for pickling/canning whole; sweet and tender, good for containers and shallow soil; direct-sow preferred (dislikes root disturbance); edible root.

packets.name: Oceanside Spinach Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 4-6 wks before last frost; succession every 2-3 wks; again in late Aug for fall crop
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct sow outdoors around late Apr (South Deerfield) or early May (Conway hilltown); spinach tolerates light frost. Sow again late Aug for fall harvest before Oct 1 first frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Baby greens ready ~25 days; full leaves 40-60 days. Bolt-prone in heat — shade-cloth or cut-and-come-again extends season. Disease-resistant, easy-to-clean leaves.

packets.name: Matador Spinach Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 4-6 wks before last frost as soon as soil is workable; succession every 2-3 wks; resow late summer for fall
sow_profile.zone_notes: Cool-season crop: direct sow early April once soil is workable and again in late August for a fall crop. Matador is very cold-hardy—fall-sown plants can overwinter under row cover in 5b/6a; hilltown Conway lags the valley by a week or two.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Smooth dark-green leaves; bolt-resistant/slow to bolt in heat; very cold-hardy; eat as baby green or mature; dislikes transplant—direct sow.

packets.name: Pink Banana Winter Squash Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil is 70-85°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Long-season C. maxima (100-120 days) is tight in our ~120-135 day frost-free window—start indoors in biodegradable pots ~2-3 wks before May 20 and transplant once soil warms after frost. Sprawling 12-15 ft vines need room; harvest before the Oct 1 frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. maxima; huge 10-12 lb, 18-24" salmon-pink storage fruit on 12-15 ft vines; dislikes root disturbance—use biodegradable pots; needs warm soil; good keeper.

packets.name: Pennsylvania Dutch Crookneck Winter Squash Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil is 70-85°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Long-season C. moschata (~105 days) fits our ~120-135 day window with little margin—start indoors in biodegradable pots ~2-3 wks before May 20 and transplant after soil warms. Vigorous vines; harvest and cure before the Oct 1 frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. moschata; heirloom long-necked crookneck with sweet, fine-grained flesh and small seed cavity; excellent storage; dislikes transplant—use biodegradable pots; needs warm soil.

packets.name: Red Kuri Winter Squash Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil is 70-85°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: At ~95 days this C. maxima fits our ~120-135 day season; direct sow 1-2 wks after May 20 when soil hits 70°F, or start indoors 2-3 wks early in biodegradable pots for insurance. Harvest and cure before the Oct 1 frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. maxima (Hokkaido/Uchiki type); 3-4 lb teardrop reddish-orange fruit with nutty, smooth flesh; good storage; dislikes transplant—use biodegradable pots.

packets.name: Javelin Parsnip Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 2-3 wks before to around last frost, once soil is workable; single main sowing
sow_profile.zone_notes: Sow early (late April-May) to fit the long 110-day season within our frost-free window; use fresh seed and keep the bed moist through slow germination. Leave roots in the ground and harvest after the first fall frosts, which sweeten them; F1 canker resistance lets them hold longer.
sow_profile.packet_notes: F1 hybrid, roots to 10 in. with strong canker resistance; sweetens after frost; direct-sow only (long taproot dislikes transplant); slow to germinate so use fresh seed and keep evenly moist; edible root.

packets.name: Green Globe Improved Artichoke Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Grown as an annual in 5b/6a (not winter-hardy here). Start indoors ~10-12 wks before May 20, then vernalize—set seedlings out for 10-14 days at ~45-50°F—to trick them into first-year budding; transplant ~2-4 wks before last frost since young plants tolerate light frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Cynara scolymus; REQUIRES vernalization (10-14 days at ~45-50°F) to form edible buds the first year in cold zones; perennial only ~zone 7+; edible flower buds, striking blue ornamental thistle and pollinator plant if left to bloom.

packets.name: Long Island Improved Brussels Sprouts Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: sow indoors/out in late spring to early summer for a fall harvest
sow_profile.zone_notes: Grow as a long-season fall crop—start indoors ~4-6 wks before setting out and transplant around early July so the 90-100 day heads mature into the cool of fall. Very frost-tolerant; light frosts after Oct 1 actually sweeten the sprouts, so harvest continues past first frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Heirloom; compact ~24" stalks yielding 75-100 firm 1-2" sprouts; frost improves flavor—harvest after light frosts; heavy feeder; tall stalks may need staking.

packets.name: Back to Black Viola Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Cool-season; start indoors ~mid-March (8-10 wks before the May 20 last frost) and transplant out while nights are still cool, or start in midsummer for fall bloom. Tolerates light frost; perennial only in zone 6+, so treat as a short-lived annual up in the Conway hilltown.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Near-black 3/4" flowers; germinates best in darkness (barely cover seed); compact bedding/container viola; deadhead to prolong bloom; edible flowers.

packets.name: Chocolate Morning Glory Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil ≥65°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season vine; nick/soak seed and direct-sow after May 20 once soil is warm, or start indoors 4-6 wks earlier in biodegradable pots (dislikes root disturbance). Blooms midsummer to frost; give a trellis in a full-sun spot.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Hard seed coat—soak 12-24 hrs or scarify before sowing; 4-5" rosy-chocolate blooms on 8-10' vine with variegated foliage; pollinator draw; seed is toxic if ingested.

packets.name: Broken Colors Four o'Clock Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil is warm
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season; direct-sow groups of 3 seeds after May 20 or start indoors 6-8 wks earlier. Fast-filling for borders; blooms afternoon/evening from midsummer to frost. Tuberous roots are root-hardy only in warmer zones—treat as an annual here or lift tubers to overwinter.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Fragrant (lilac/jasmine) bicolored mottled 2" tubular flowers opening late afternoon; large seed easy to handle; self-sows; evening-pollinator (moth) magnet; seeds/roots toxic if eaten.

packets.name: Grandpa Ott's Morning Glory Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil ≥65°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season heirloom vine; soak/nick seed and direct-sow after May 20 once soil warms, or start indoors 4-6 wks earlier in peat pots. Deep-purple star-throated blooms midsummer to frost on a full-sun trellis; self-sows readily.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Hard seed coat—soak 12-24 hrs or nick before sowing; classic deep royal-purple bloom with magenta star throat; vigorous 8-12' vine; pollinator/hummingbird draw; toxic seed.

packets.name: Heavenly Blue Morning Glory Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil ≥65°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season; day-length-sensitive so blooms heavily from mid/late August to frost—start indoors 4-6 wks before May 20 (peat pots) to bank a longer season before our early-Oct frost, or soak-and-direct-sow after last frost. Full-sun trellis.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Hard seed coat—soak 12-24 hrs or scarify; sky-blue 4-5" trumpets with white/yellow throat; day-length-sensitive (late bloomer); 8-12' vine; pollinator draw; toxic seed.

packets.name: Column Blend Stock Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: early spring, a few weeks before last frost while soil is cool
sow_profile.zone_notes: Cool-season cut flower; start indoors ~mid-March (8-10 wks before May 20) and transplant while nights are cool—won't set buds if seedlings run warm (keep ≤75°F). Tolerates light frost; succession-sow every 2-3 wks for spring/early-summer stems before summer heat.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Press seed onto surface—needs light to germinate; keep seedlings cool (≤75°F) or blooming fails; fragrant clove-scented double columnar spikes 24-30" for cutting; deer-resistant.

packets.name: Pacific Giants Blend Delphinium Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Short-lived perennial, reliably hardy through our zone 5b-6a (hardy to zone 3). Cold-stratify seed ~1-2 wks in the fridge, then start indoors 6-8 wks before May 20 and transplant; usually blooms its second year (late spring-early summer), sometimes first-year. Stake the tall spires; often lives only 2-3 years.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Cold-stratify seed (1-2 wks moist, refrigerated) and germinate cool in darkness for best rates; short-lived perennial; 3-6' spires need staking; blooms late spring-early summer; all parts toxic if eaten; pollinator/hummingbird draw.

packets.name: Black Velvet Nasturtium Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil 55-65°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Direct-sow after May 20, or start indoors only 2-4 wks earlier in biodegradable pots (roots resent transplanting). Blooms best in lean soil and cooler weather—may pause in midsummer heat and rebound in fall. Not frost-hardy.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Soak seed 12-24 hrs to speed germination (hard coat); deep near-black velvety blooms; roots dislike transplant—sow in peat pots or direct; edible flowers/leaves; lean soil = more flowers; aphid trap crop; pollinator draw.

packets.name: Padron Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights early-to-mid April (6-8 wks before the ~May 20 last frost); transplant after May 20 once soil is ≥60°F. Harvest most pods young and green for tapas; Conway hilltown 5b growers have ample season since pods are picked immature.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; 500-2,500 SHU, mild but ~5-10% run hot when small. Harvested green (1-3 in) for classic blistered Spanish tapas; ripens to red and hotter if left on the plant.

packets.name: Ghost Bhut Jolokia Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: A long-season super-hot: start indoors mid-March (8-10 wks before ~May 20) with bottom heat, transplant late May once nights stay above 55°F. At ~100 days from transplant it just fits our ~120-135 day season; Conway 5b growers should start on the early end and use a warm, sheltered spot or container.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum chinense; over 1,000,000 SHU (one of the world's hottest). 2.5-3 in bumpy pods ripen green to scarlet/orange-red; use sparingly in sauces, powders, and extracts. Slow to germinate.

packets.name: Scotch Bonnet Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Long-season chinense: start indoors mid-March (8-10 wks before ~May 20) with bottom heat, transplant late May in the warmest bed. At 90-120 days it pushes the limit of our season, so Conway 5b growers should grow in containers that can be moved or given season extension to ripen fully.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum chinense; 100,000-325,000 SHU. 1.5 in puckered pods ripen green to red with fruity, smoky flavor; a staple of Caribbean cooking (jerk, hot sauce). Start 8-10 wks before last frost.

packets.name: Habanero Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Long-season chinense: start indoors mid-March (8-10 wks before ~May 20) with bottom heat, transplant late May once soil is warm. At ~100 days it fits our ~120-135 day season if started early; Conway 5b growers should favor a container or the warmest, most sheltered bed.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum chinense; 100,000-350,000 SHU. 2.5 in pods ripen green to orange-red with prized fruity flavor; use in salsas and hot sauces. Slow, warmth-dependent germination.

packets.name: Thai Hot Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors mid-to-late March (8-10 wks before ~May 20), transplant after May 20. Compact 8 in mounding plants are an excellent container and patio crop and can be potted up and overwintered indoors on a sunny sill.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; 50,000-100,000 SHU. Compact 8 in plants covered in upright 1.5-3 in pods ripening green to red; edible and ornamental, ideal for containers. Staple of Thai cooking.

packets.name: NuMex Lemon Spice Jalapeño Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors early-to-mid April (6-8 wks before ~May 20), transplant after May 20. At ~65 days it matures comfortably within our season, a reliable choice even for Conway 5b gardens.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; 2,500-5,000 SHU. Jalapeno-shaped 2-3 in pods ripen green to bright yellow with a citrusy tang; bred by the NM Chile Pepper Institute. Use fresh in salsas.

packets.name: Serrano Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors early-to-mid April (6-8 wks before ~May 20), transplant after May 20 into the warmest bed. At 75-90 days it fits our season; pick green for pico or let ripen red where the season allows.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; 10,000-20,000 SHU. Slender 2-3 in thick-fleshed pods ripen green to red; crisp and bright, classic for pico de gallo and fresh salsas.

packets.name: Jimmy Nardello Sweet Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors early-to-mid April (6-8 wks before ~May 20), transplant after May 20. At 80-90 days it ripens fully within our season; a heavy-yielding heirloom worth the warmest bed in Conway 5b gardens.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; sweet, essentially no heat (~0 SHU). Long 6-12 in tapering pods ripen green to glossy deep red; the classic sweet Italian frying pepper, 1887 heirloom.

packets.name: Red and Yellow Blend Biquinho Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors mid-March; transplant after May 20 (valley). Long-season pepper — western MA's 120-day window is tight. Prioritize early indoor start and warm transplant site. Can be overwintered indoors as a container plant.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum chinense. Mild, only 1,000-2,000 Scoville units. Teardrop-shaped fruits 0.75-1.25" ripen to red or golden yellow. Brazilian specialty pepper. Long season; needs warmth to produce well. Can overwinter indoors.

packets.name: Ancho/Poblano Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors early-to-mid April (6-8 wks before ~May 20), transplant after May 20. At 65-75 days fresh poblanos mature easily here; leaving pods to ripen red-brown for drying as ancho takes the full season, so favor a warm bed in Conway 5b.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; mild 1,000-2,000 SHU. 3-6 in pods are dark green (poblano, fresh) ripening to reddish-brown (ancho, dried). Use fresh for rellenos/roasting, dried for mole.

packets.name: Early Jalapeño Chile Pepper Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors early-to-mid April (6-8 wks before ~May 20), transplant after May 20. Bred for cooler climates and quick at ~63 days, it is one of the most reliable peppers for Conway 5b and short-season hilltown gardens; does well in containers too.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; 2,500-5,000 SHU. 3 in pods ripen dark green to red; cool-climate-adapted and early. Use fresh green for salsa and poppers or ripen red for sweeter heat.

packets.name: Favourite Blend French Marigold Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil ≥70°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season; start indoors 4-6 wks before May 20 for early color or direct-sow once soil warms after last frost. Fast and forgiving; compact 10-12" plants edge beds/veg rows and bloom nonstop to first fall frost. Not frost-hardy.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Compact 10-12" single-row blooms in gold/yellow/red/bicolor; very easy from seed; deadhead for continuous bloom; classic veg-garden companion/pest-deterrent; pollinator draw; edible petals.

packets.name: Naughty Marietta French Marigold Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil ≥70°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season heirloom; start indoors 4-6 wks before May 20 or direct-sow after last frost once soil is warm. Reliable, quick single blooms from summer to frost on 12-16" plants; excellent veg-garden companion. Not frost-hardy.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Heirloom single golden-yellow blooms splashed maroon/mahogany; 12-16" tall; very easy and quick from seed; deadhead for continuous bloom; pollinator draw; edible petals; classic companion plant.

packets.name: Red Metamorph French Marigold Seeds
packets.source: Botanical Interests online order #350019 (confirmed 2026-07-08, received 2026-07-18); July 2026 intake.

sow_profile.direct_sow_timing: 1-2 wks after last frost when soil 70-80°F
sow_profile.zone_notes: Warm-season; start indoors 4-6 wks before May 20 or direct-sow after last frost once soil hits 70-80°F. Stout, dense 2-3' plants; blooms shift burgundy↔yellow-splashed with our cool-to-warm swings, so western-MA's cool springs/falls show the deepest reds. Not frost-hardy.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Color-shifting 1.5-2" scalloped blooms—deep burgundy in cool weather, yellow splashes when warm; stout dense 2-3' plant; deadhead for continuous bloom; pollinator draw; edible petals.

packets.name: Glacier Tomato
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Extra-early and notably cold-tolerant: start indoors under lights late March-early April, 6-8 wks before the ~May 20 valley frost; can transplant a bit earlier than most tomatoes with cloche/row-cover protection. Ideal first-ripe and short-season pick for the Conway hilltown.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Determinate. Very cold/cool-tolerant, among the earliest to ripen. Compact bush, 1.25" red saladette fruit with unusually good early-season flavor; little staking needed.

packets.name: Manitoba Tomato
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Bred for short cool prairie seasons, so it suits both the South Deerfield valley and the Conway hilltown: start indoors under lights late March-early April, 6-8 wks before the ~May 20 frost; transplant early June. Reliable early yield before the ~Oct 1 fall frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Determinate. Early, cool-season prairie heirloom (Morden Research Station, Manitoba, 1950s). Vigorous bush setting clusters of 4-6 oz smooth deep-red fruit; needs little support.

packets.name: White Habanero Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights ~10-12 wks before the May 20 last frost; transplant only after nights stay above 55F, early June, once soil is warm. Frost-tender long-season chinense; Conway hilltowns should push transplant to mid-June and can overwinter a plant indoors.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense. Scoville ~300,000-500,000 SHU. Small 2" lantern pods ripen green to creamy white; hot, fruity, ornamental. Slow-germinating; use bottom heat 80-85F. Compact bushy plant good for containers. Culinary heat and salsa.

packets.name: Trinidad Scorpion Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: A superhot needing the longest runway here: start indoors 10-12 wks before May 20 and don't transplant until soil is warm in June. Marginal for our ~120-135 day season, so start early, use black mulch/warmest bed, and consider overwintering a plant indoors.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense, superhot. Scoville ~1,200,000-2,000,000 SHU. Wrinkled stinger-tailed pods ripen to searing red. Very slow, erratic germination; needs 80-85F bottom heat. Handle with gloves. Extract-grade heat for sauces/powder.

packets.name: Thai Volcano Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights on a heat mat early-mid March (8-10 wks before the ~May 20 valley frost, later up in Conway); transplant only after soil warms and nights stay above 55F, usually early June. Frost-tender; needs the full warm season to ripen red.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; ~50,000-100,000 SHU; fiery Thai type ripening green to bright red on compact 12-18in bushes; heavy yields of small hot pods for Asian cooking, drying, and sauces.

packets.name: Tepin Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: This wild chile germinates slowly and erratically (weeks, not days) so start indoors very early, late February-early March, on a heat mat at 80-85F with patience; transplant only after solid warmth in June. Slow-growing and heat-loving, it is a good candidate to pot up and overwinter indoors as a tender perennial in our short season.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum var. glabriusculum; wild chile ~50,000-100,000 SHU; tiny round pods ripening green to red on a bushy 2-3ft plant; essentially the same wild pepper as Chiltepin. Germinates slowly/erratically; needs warmth and patience; edible, bird-favored, considered a mother pepper of cultivated chiles.

packets.name: Thai Hot Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights on a heat mat mid-March; transplant early June after nights stay above 55F. Compact and heavy-setting, it does well in containers on a warm patio and makes an attractive potted plant to overwinter indoors; frost-tender.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; ~50,000-100,000 SHU; many small conical pods held upright, ripening green to red on compact mounding plants; ornamental-edible, excellent for drying and Thai cooking.

packets.name: Takanotsume Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights on a heat mat mid-March (8-10 wks before the ~May 20 valley frost, later in Conway); transplant early June once nights stay above 55F. Relatively quick to mature, so it ripens reliably even in our short season; frost-tender.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; ~30,000-50,000 SHU; slim talon-shaped pods held upright above the foliage, ripening green to bright red; classic Japanese drying chile (togarashi) for flakes and oils.

packets.name: Tabasco Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: A frutescens type that loves heat and needs a long season, so start indoors early-mid March on a heat mat (75-85F) and transplant only after soil is warm in June. Ripens later than annuum chiles; potting up and overwintering indoors helps in our short 120-135 day season.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum frutescens; ~30,000-50,000 SHU; small upright pods ripening green through yellow-orange to red on a bushy 2-4ft plant; the classic hot-sauce pepper, clean sharp heat.

packets.name: Shishito Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights on a heat mat mid-March; transplant early June once nights hold above 55F. Quick and heavy-bearing, harvested young and green it produces early and long through our summer; frost-tender.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; mild ~50-200 SHU (an occasional pod spikes hotter); thin-walled wrinkled pods harvested green (ripen red if left); the classic blistering/tempura pepper, prolific and easy.

packets.name: Serrano Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors mid-March (8-10 wks before the ~May 20 last frost) and transplant only after frost passes and soil is ≥60°F, late May in the valley or early June in the Conway hilltown. No frost tolerance; a warm, sheltered bed maximizes ripening in our 120-135 day season.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. 10,000-25,000 SHU. Ripens green to red, commonly used green; thin-walled Mexican chile for salsa/pico de gallo, not a drying type.

packets.name: Serrano Huasteca Pepper

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors mid-March (8-10 wks before the ~May 20 last frost); transplant late May in the valley or early June in the Conway hilltown once frost is past and soil is ≥60°F. No frost tolerance; harvest green through summer with a red flush by our Oct 1 frost.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. Up to 25,000 SHU. Bullet-shaped ~2.5" pods ripen green to red, typically used green in salsa; not a drying type.

packets.name: Red Mushroom Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: A C. chinense with slow germination and a long season, so start earliest, late February to early March (10-12 wks before ~May 20 frost), under consistent warmth (80-90°F soil). sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense. ~25,000-50,000 SHU. Distinctive mushroom/squash-shaped pods ripen green to bright red; rare Jamaican-origin chile, thick-fleshed for sauces and pickling.

packets.name: Red Hot Cherry Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. 2,500-5,000 SHU. Round ~1.5" cherry-shaped pods ripen green to red; thick-walled, popular pickled, stuffed, or fresh.

packets.name: Purple Cayenne Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. 30,000-50,000 SHU. Slender 3-6" pods ripen green to purple to bright red; ornamental and culinary, good fresh, dried, or pickled.

packets.name: Pueblo "Mosco" Chile Pepper

packets.name: Peter Pepper

packets.name: Pepperoncini Sweet Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. 100-500 SHU (mild). Sweet, tangy 2-3" Italian/Greek pickling pepper harvested young green-yellow, ripening red; low-heat, crisp for pickling and salads.

packets.name: Padron Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. Scoville 500-2,500 SHU (mild, roulette hotter ones). Harvested green; ripens red if left on. Famous Spanish blistered/fried tapas pepper.

packets.name: Lemon Habanero Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense (aka Yellow Habanero). Scoville ~100,000-350,000 SHU. Lantern pods ripen green to lemon yellow with citrus/apricot aroma. Ornamental, container-friendly; salsa, sauce, marinades. Slow germ, bottom heat 80-85F.

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum, Pennsylvania Dutch heirloom. Scoville ~5,000-30,000 SHU. Small chicken-heart-shaped bumpy pods ripen green to red (also a yellow strain). Rarely eaten raw; traditional for pickling and pepper vinegar.

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. 3,000-17,000 SHU (classic serrano heat). Thin-walled 2.5-3" pods ripen light green to scarlet red; used green, very productive.

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. Scoville ~2,500-10,000 SHU (jalapeno-like). Glossy conical pods ripen green to orange to bright red, fruitier and hotter when red. Fresh use, salsa, pickling, hot sauce.

packets.name: Fish Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum, variegated heirloom. Scoville ~5,000-30,000 SHU. Striped pods ripen white-with-green-stripes to orange to red; foliage is white-green mottled. Culinary (historic Chesapeake fish/shellfish dishes) and ornamental.

packets.name: Baby Bell Pepper Mix

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum, sweet (0 SHU). Miniature ~1" bells in red, yellow and brown/chocolate, thick sweet flesh. Heavy set on 24" plants; great for containers and stuffing.

packets.name: Big Jim Hot Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: Start indoors under lights mid-March, ~8-10 wks before the ~May 20 valley frost; transplant early June into warm soil. Long-fruited plants may need staking. Not frost tolerant; harvest green chiles before the ~Oct 1 first frost or let a few ripen red.
sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum. Scoville 500-2,500 SHU (mild-medium). Enormous 8-12" Hatch-type green chiles ripening red; classic roasting/relleno chile. NMSU heirloom.

packets.name: Birdseye Chili Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.zone_notes: A heat-demanding frutescens/annuum type with a long season, so start indoors very early (late February-early March) on a heat mat and transplant only after full warmth in June. Slow to ripen in our short season; pot up and overwinter indoors to reliably finish a crop.
sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum frutescens (sometimes listed as annuum); ~50,000-100,000 SHU; tiny slender pods held upright, ripening green to red on a bushy plant; the classic Southeast-Asian bird chile, potent fresh or dried.

packets.name: Buena Mulata Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. annuum, purple heirloom cayenne. Scoville ~30,000-50,000 SHU. Slim pods ripen purple to orange to brown to red. Ornamental and edible; dried powder, flakes, fresh. Traced to artist Horace Pippin.

packets.name: Chinese 5 Color Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; ~5,000-30,000 SHU; small upright conical pods passing through purple, cream, yellow, orange and red simultaneously on dark-purple foliage; ornamental-edible, heat increasing as pods ripen.

packets.name: Chiltepin Pepper

sow_profile.zone_notes: Like Tepin, germination is slow and erratic over several weeks, so start indoors very early (late February-early March) on a heat mat at 80-85F; transplant after full warmth in June. sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum var. glabriusculum; wild chile ~50,000-100,000 SHU; tiny (~0.3in) round pods ripening green to red on a bush to ~4ft; near-identical to Tepin (Tepin and Chiltepin are two names for the same wild species). sow_profile.packet_notes: Capsicum annuum; ~15,000-30,000 SHU (can run hotter); slender curved pods ripening green to bright red on tall plants; the classic Mexican drying chile, dried whole for salsas and oils.

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense. Scoville 500-1,000 SHU (very mild, fruity). Teardrop 'little beak' pods ripen bright red; smoky-fruity, usually pickled in vinegar or eaten raw.

packets.name: Chocolate Habanero Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense. Scoville ~300,000-450,000 SHU (up to ~577k). Wrinkled pods ripen green to deep mahogany brown. Rich, smoky-fruity; prized for hot sauce and salsa. Slow to germinate; bottom heat 80-85F.

packets.name: Aji Cito Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. baccatum. Scoville ~10,000-100,000 SHU. Heavy sets of small ~2" pods ripen green to yellow to sunset orange. Fruity baccatum flavor; fresh use, sauces, ornamental. Slow germ, bottom heat 80-85F.

packets.name: Biquinho Yellow Pepper
packets.source: Mary's Heirloom Seeds online order (HOMESTEAD discount); July 2026 intake. Received 2026-07-17.

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. chinense. Scoville 500-1,000 SHU (barely-there heat, tropical-fruity). Marble-sized pointed 'little beak' pods ripen yellow; eaten fresh or pickled.

packets.name: Aji Habanero Pepper

sow_profile.packet_notes: C. baccatum. Scoville ~1,000-23,000 SHU (mild-moderate). Slim 2.5" pods ripen green to pale yellow to pale orange. Smoky habanero-like flavor with light heat; fresh use, salsa. Slow germ, bottom heat 80-85F.
